title: An Interpretable Multi-Modal Deep Learning Framework for Real-Time Detection of COVID-19 and Viral Pneumonia Using X-Ray and CT Imaging
content: The global outbreak of COVID-19 has underscored the urgent need for fast, accurate, and understandable diagnostic tools that can support healthcare workers in making quick and informed decisions. Traditional deep learning models have mostly depended on a single type of medical image - either chest X-rays or CT scans. However, these approaches often fall short due to limited sensitivity, overlapping features, and poor adaptability across diverse patient data. To address these challenges, we propose ExplainFusion-Net - a new deep learning model designed to intelligently combine both X-ray and CT images to more accurately detect COVID-19 and viral pneumonia. This framework uses two parallel CNN streams to extract unique features from each imaging type, then blends them using an attention-based fusion layer that focuses on the most important diagnostic cues. The classification is finalized using a softmax-enabled fully connected layer. The model was trained and tested using real-world datasets such as COVIDx CXR2, the COVID-19 Radiography Database, COVID-CTset, and COVID-19 CT Scans. We also applied techniques like data augmentation, class balancing, and dropout regularization to ensure the model works well across various conditions and avoids overfitting. The results speak for themselves: ExplainFusion-Net achieved 95% training accuracy, 93% validation accuracy, and an AUC of 1.00, indicating perfect performance in distinguishing between cases. The model made only 35 errors out of 400 predictions, with an F1-score above 0.92, confirming its strength in both sensitivity and precision. Moreover, built-in visualization tools like ROC curves and confusion matrices improve transparency and trust in the model’s decisions - critical for real-world clinical use. Overall, ExplainFusion-Net shows strong promise as a reliable and explainable AI system for frontline pandemic diagnostics, opening the door to future advances in multi-modal medical imaging solutions.
